blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Formal letter writing requires strict adherence to standardized layouts and presentation guidelines.
Mastering the structural format of formal letters is essential for descriptive sections in competitive exams.
Effective strategy involves maintaining a formal tone, clear objective, and precise language.

blocks.content: A formal letter follows a strict structure. The following elements must be present in the correct order:
1. Sender's Address (top right or top left depending on style)
6. Body: Paragraph 1 — Introduction / Purpose; Paragraph 2 — Main Content / Details; Paragraph 3 — Request / Conclusion
7. Complimentary Close: 'Yours faithfully' (when salutation is 'Dear Sir/Madam')
Common Types of Letters in Banking Exams:
• Letters to the Bank Manager (complaint, request, information)
• Letters to the Editor (of a newspaper — on banking, financial, social issues)
• Letters to RBI/Government Officials (policy suggestions, implementation issues)

items: Always follow the exact sequence: Sender's Address, Date, Receiver's Address, Subject, Salutation, Body, and Complimentary Close.
Avoid using informal contractions, abbreviations, or conversational expressions in formal letter writing.

blocks.content: • Letters from Branch Manager to Head Office (reporting, proposals)
• Letters from an Officer to a Borrower (notice, reminder, recovery)

Examiner's Tip: Always read the instruction carefully. Note who is writing, to whom, and on what topic. Never confuse the sender and recipient. In 'To the Editor' letters, sign as 'A Concerned Citizen' or your exam roll number if instructed.
